# Journal Entry 2:

Topic Covered: The forecasting problem, Exploring a time series and how decomposition works

What I did: Went over the lecture 2 in Sulaiman's class as well as attempted to do a tutorial on how these concepts work and how to apply them.

What I learnt: I learnt about the difference between forecasting as well as what predicting is and how that are not the same, forecasting is all about projecting into the future based on past data. There are a lot of factors to take into this based on the complexity of the time series data. I also learnt that forecasting will be determines by the research question and need four conditions to be satisfied. Also how the Forecast-Goal-Plan is a feedback loop. I also learnt that our forecast horizons will depend on certain hings such as how long the period is. One concept that i learnt that I think is very important is that we need to break our time series into its separate components and then we model on them separately and put them together. It can be decomposed into the trend, the seasonality, the cyclical component and then the Irregularity. They can be combined in linear or multiplicative form. I also learnt how to identify each one such as a season, trend, cyclic and the irregular components

# Journal Entry 3:

Date: 17 August 2026

Topic Covered: Forecasting methods, and Cross validation techniques and performance metrics

What I did: Went over the lecture content and attended the Lecture on these concepts.

What I learnt: I learnt about the 4 different benchmark forecasting method, and how it is important to do more than 1 method even thought the are different recommended forecasts for different time series with components. There is no better method it all depends on the data as well as the question we are trying to answer. It seems that for time series there can be quite a bit of subjectivity and it comes down to your data and the question you are trying to answer. Similar to cross sectional data residuals and performance measures are found to be calculated the same except the out of sample error cannot be randomized, it needs to be ordered.

We also covered cross validation and the difference in regards to cross sectional data and time series data. Time series data we cannot do a random split, reason being that successive. I also learnt that every training set must precede the validation set or else there will be temporal leakage. The lecture also covered. The lecture also covered the accuracy measured used such as MAE, RMSE, MAPE AND MASE and as well as when to use which metric. The lecture then covered the walk forward, expanding windo validation and sliding window validation.

Difficulties or Open questions: I am unsure about the fundamental difference between expanding window and walk forward validation.

Next steps: Do a tutorial on how to do cross validation for a time series as well as do the excercise in the slides on page 72 of the slides.

# Journal Entry 4:

Date: 19 August 2026

Topic Covered: Lag and Lead operators, stationary, white noise, and restoring stationary.

What I did: Attended the Lecture and went over the slides as well as my notes.

What I learnt: I learnt about the lead and lag of time series data with the lag being we record the measure today as yesterdays and the lead being we record today measure as tomorrows measure. I also learnt about strict stationarity and weak stationarity and how the aim is to get the model to stationary to be able to then model and make inference, so we difference to remove trends, seasonality. I also learnt about ergodicity which means that the time series fluctuates around a mean value, which indicates stationarity which is the goal. If the data is stationary then we can model, forecast correctly and so on. Lastly the lecture went through how to get the data to be stationary and how to determine how much differencing is required to remove trend in the data.

Difficulties or Open questions: Still struggling to understand why we need to have a lead and lags as well. I kind of understand that lags help identify possible correlation but lead i'm not sure. I also need to go over the notation for the the algebra of lags and leads.

Next steps: Go over the Lags and leads for more understanding and do a tutorial on the difference techniques for restoring stationarity.

# Journal Entry 5:

Date: 24 August 2026

Topic Covered: MA(1), AR(1), ACF, PCF, ARMA models, Differencing, ARIMA, SARIMA, Box Jenkins loop. We also went through the data sets we can use for out portfolio projects during the lecture.

What I did: Went over the lecture as well as my notes that I made during the lecture on the linear conditional mean models.

What I learnt: I learnt about Moving averages which looks at correlated errors, and the Auto regressive model which looks at observations are related, and ARMA models which are a combination of MA and AR models. I learnt about the mean and variance for each of these models as well as the properties. I also learnt about what the plots looks like for each type of the ARMA models.

The other thing I learnt was the ACF and PCF plots which help determine the number of lags depending on whether the values lie in between a region. I think one thing that was interesting is that even if we choose the number of lags we also need to look at the performance of an extra lag more and one less to see which one aligns more with the data. This lecture also covered overdifferencing and how if we do it will over-inflate the values emphasizing the importance of differencing only when necessary.

ARIMA models includes the differencing element which was covered in the lecture as well and how certain specifications of ARIMA collapse to an AR(1), MA(1), ARMA(1,1), random walk, given the fact there is no constant value. The lecture also covered, checking residuals and the box Jenkins workflow of identifying an adequate model.

Lastly, the lecture had a look at SARIMA models which adds a seasonal component in the time series data.This means there would need to be differencing for the seasonal elements as well.

Difficulties or Open questions: I would like to determine how they got to the mean and variance values for these models. In the slide we only get given the values.

Next steps: Research and define my project to do a comparative study between these models.
